title: R' Yehudah the Circumciser
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Shabbat 130b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.130b.6), R' Hoshaya says, “I asked R' Yehudah the Circumciser,” etc. The related exchange appears in [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 19:1 (Hyman cites 18:1)](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.19.1.2). [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.130b.6.2) explains that he was a mohel. Hyman understands this Hoshaya to be R' Oshaya, R' Chiya’s student, which would place Yehudah among the last Tannaim, after Rabbi. The supplied notice then breaks off: “and there is…”[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s text ends after “and there is.”
The linked Rashi glosses the epithet as someone who circumcises infants.

Hyman’s printed notice cites Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 18:1 and breaks off after “and there is.” The matching exchange in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 19:1 has R’ Hoshaya say “we asked” and “he told us,” in a discussion of a dead-end alley. The consulted Shabbat 130b has R’ Oshaya say “I asked” and “he told me,” and Rashi explains that Yehudah circumcised infants. The identification of Hoshaya with Chiya’s student and the resulting date are Hyman’s inferences.
